chapter: Mutes, influences and the blues singers
title: How Ma Rainey compared as a performer with the Smiths
summary: Ma was not as dynamic or loud as Bessie or Clara, but was an early Southern star who ran several touring shows that left performers stranded.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Do the records that we have of her give any indication of the effect she has as a performer? Because they're -- most of the records are kind of -- a little bit dim. They're old, pre-electric recordings. Was she a really -- an electrifying kind of performer when she got on, or not?
No. To answer you -- wait just a minute -- to answer you, because when you say electrifying a person will -- bang! -- when those people really start out. Clara Smith, Bessie Smith --
No, she did her thing, but -- I mean you know, like when Bessie open her mouth, I mean you could hear Bessie all -- from here to Florida, man. You know.
Well what was it that Ma had that made her so --
-- have such a following? Why was she so great?
I would say -- I think Ma, being one of the first, before Bessie and those people, I mean in the

South, anyway, I would say, who was famous, and I -- she wasn't more famous than Bessie, and after Smith. She was not! But I think Ma got on record, maybe. Maybe, now, now I'm speculating, before Bessie, Clara, and those people, maybe. But Ma did her thing, but she wasn't -- she wasn't into the Smith's, I mean when it came to banging it out and punch, you know, and being dynamic, because they says well all right, take in on loud, here come Ma with one of those A notes. She was -- and she had the only show. She had several shows that she took out with her. You know, several girls, comedians, the same type of thing that most people had in those days, with the show business.
Chorus girls, comedians, and dancers, and all of them got stranded, and owed everybody.
